added: Switch between your lists from the editor's toolbar, without leaving the one you're in.
Recent changes now name what happened — "Removed Nunatak quilt liner", "Swapped Durston X-Mid 2 for Big Agnes Copper Spur" — instead of "Edited 1 item".
changed: The toolbar now says when your list was last edited, and only mentions syncing when there's something to say.
The gear vault's sign-in prompt is one line now, and reads the same on the vault page and beside a list.
A folder's controls now stay visible instead of appearing on hover.
On a shared list, the export formats group under one "Export" item, matching the editor.
fixed: The gear vault no longer offers to save a list's gear when you're signed out, which spent the one time it asks about that list.
On a phone, an item's gear type now sits tight under its row instead of floating below it.
The footer no longer offers a gear vault link when you're signed out.

added: Track calories on food and fuel, and see the total for your list.
Rows now keep the unit you typed, whatever the list's unit is.
Save any item to your gear vault straight from its row.
Save a whole category to your vault and drop it into a new list.
Send feedback about a list from the editor's actions menu.
Give a list its trip dates.
Shared lists now show the calories on each food item, not just the total.
Reach your account from the toolbar while you're editing a list — sign in, open your gear vault, or sign out without leaving the page.
changed: Worn and consumable are now two toggles on the row, each opening its own small panel.
Row actions now stay visible instead of appearing only on hover.
Sharing now lives in one panel — both links, replacing the edit link, and recent changes.
Export options group together in the actions menu.
Icons have a new, rounder look.
List and folder names now show when they can be edited.
On a phone, saving an item to your gear vault has moved into the row's ⋯ menu, so the row's controls fit.
On a phone, the trail link's card now opens when you press the link name, instead of sitting under the title all the time.
Each row's weight unit now shows a small arrow, so you can see it can be changed.
The gear vault's search and “Add folder” now look and work like the editor's.
Trip dates now read as "September 6–9, 2026".
Send feedback moved out of the footer, into the ⋯ menu on the list you're looking at.
Recent changes in the sharing panel now slides open like the app's other disclosures.
The sharing panel's Copy button is filled instead of outlined, matching the rest of the chrome.
fixed: On a phone, swiping the gear vault sheet now scrolls the gear inside it instead of the list behind it.
Ungrouped items now sit the same distance from their heading as items in a folder.
On a phone, the trip date picker and the sharing panel now open fully on screen.
On the narrowest phones, a row's buttons now wrap onto their own line instead of running off the edge.
Arrow keys now move through the trip date picker, and picking commits the day you landed on.
Importing a CSV no longer locks every row to a single unit.
Weights line up in a column on a shared list, whatever unit each row is in.
On a touch tablet, a row's buttons no longer overlap the worn and consumable toggles.
Your gear vault now opens to its empty state on a brand-new account, instead of a connection error.
"Get a new link" on an expired sign-in link now takes you to the sign-in form.
The clear-search, dismiss, and move-to-folder controls are easier to tap on a phone.
Delete account now reads in the site's own ink, clear in dark mode too.
A sign-in link now removes any passkey that was set up on your account before you first signed in, and signs out whoever added it.

added: Create an account with a passkey — your face, fingerprint or screen lock, no password to pick.
Sign in with a passkey in one tap, or have a link emailed to you instead.
Set a display name and it shows under the title on lists you share or publish. Leave it blank and they stay anonymous.
Delete your account from the account page — it takes your gear vault with it, and asks separately whether to delete your lists.
Sign out everywhere, from your account page — ends every session on every device.
Mahonia emails you when a passkey is added to your account, so you find out if it wasn't you.
changed: Your gear vault now lives in an account instead of behind a link. Sign in on another device and your gear is there; clear your browser and it's still there. Building and sharing lists still needs no account.

added: Gear vaults that go unused for a long time are now cleaned up, and using the vault's link brings one back.
Drag gear straight from your vault onto the folder you want it in, instead of picking the folder first.
Your vault sits beside the list you're building and can be resized to whatever width suits you.
Reach your vault from the footer of any page.
Gear you've removed from your vault is listed under "Removed gear", so you can put a piece back.
Folders in your gear vault: gear files itself under the list folder it came from, and you can rename, sort, reorder and delete them.
Drag gear between folders in your vault.
When you edit a list you didn't start, Mahonia asks once whether its gear belongs in your vault.
Opening a gear vault link on a device that already has gear now combines the two, instead of leaving one of them behind.
Bring another device's gear vault into this one by pasting its link, without leaving the vault you're on.
Choosing Add on a list you didn't start now lets you pick which gear is yours, instead of taking all of it.
changed: Gear already in the open list shows as "Already added" in the vault, so nothing lands twice.
About and What's new are one page now.
Change the weight unit from the vault's total, the same way you do on a list.
Removing gear from your vault now offers an undo, like removing an item from a list.
The vault slides in when you open it beside a list, instead of appearing all at once.
Vault search now forgives typos and matches on gear type, like the item search does — and bolds what you typed.
The vault is now called your gear vault, everywhere it's named.
Gear rows in the vault use icons for their actions instead of a word.
The vault prompt now sits inline under the weight chart, and slides away when dismissed.
fixed: Long gear names in the vault no longer swallow the brand or knock a row out of line.
The vault panel keeps its height while you filter it, instead of collapsing as results narrow.
Opening a list someone shared with you no longer copies their gear into your vault.

changed: The trail link's card shows the destination without the https:// and www., so more of the address fits.
In the editor, tapping a trail link now opens its card instead of leaving the page — the link itself is in the card. On a shared list it still goes straight there.
The trail link's address is capped at a readable length instead of running the width of the card.
fixed: A long list name now wraps onto more lines instead of scrolling sideways out of view.
On a phone, the trail link's card now sits on its own line, so the trail's name isn't cut short and Edit stays reachable.
The toolbar's controls no longer drift to the left on a brand-new list.

added: Attach a link to the trail a list was packed for — it shows on the shared and public views, with the site's icon.
The summary now shows a carried weight — base plus consumable, the weight actually on your back — alongside the three figures it's drawn from.
Copying a list as Markdown includes the carried weight too.
Your vault: gear you put in a list is remembered in one place, ready to pull into the next list without retyping. No account — the vault is yours by link, like a list.
Add gear from your vault without typing: a panel beside the list you're building, with everything you own a click away.
Open your vault on another device with a link, the same way you already move a list.
changed: A list's name now sits at the top of the page as a proper title, instead of in the toolbar.
The trail link now brightens as you point at it, in the editor, the packing checklist and the shared views alike.
The sync state and last-edited time now sit at the left of the editor's toolbar instead of below the list name.
The pack total and the trail link now have a little more room beneath them.
fixed: Closing an item's gear-type field no longer jumps a few pixels past where it settles and snaps back.

added: A "Skip to content" link now appears on the first tab press, jumping straight past the toolbar to the list.
changed: On a shared list, each item's weight now sits closer to its name instead of drifting out to the far right of a wide window.
Item names on a shared list no longer carry a permanent underline — the search link shows itself as you move down the list.
The pack total no longer repeats itself as a "Base" figure directly underneath when everything in the list is base weight.
The About and Legal pages now sit centred in the page instead of hugging the left edge.
fixed: Edits made in the moment you leave a list no longer go missing if the connection drops on the way out.
Weights on a shared list no longer flicker into a different number format as the page finishes loading.

changed: The packing checklist's checkboxes are now drawn by the same icon set as the toolbar's packing toggle — the same square-and-tick glyph, with the tick still popping in.
The big pack-weight total at the top of a list now reads larger.
fixed: On a shared list, an item's gear type now sits snug under its name, matching the editor.

added: Every item now carries a gear type like "tent" or "trail runners" — filled in automatically when you pick it, shown as a quiet line under the product, and renamable per list.
Start a new list straight from the editor's ⋯ menu.
changed: Typing a gear name now surfaces closer name matches first, above merely-popular ones.
Editing and packing modes now ease from one to the other when you switch, instead of snapping.
Empty folders no longer draw a faint line under their name — the divider only shows between rows once you've added items.
Editing an item's name now offers its gear type right below, so gear you type in yourself can carry one too.
CSV exports carry a "Gear Type" column; older files with a "Common Name" column still import.
A group row no longer offers a gear type of its own — the group's name already is one.
fixed: Switching to packing mode no longer makes the rows taller — editing and packing keep the same row height, so the list doesn't jump on toggle.
Item notes sit the same distance below their name in shared and public lists as they do in the editor.
The “Add an item” button now lines up with your list's row spacing on phone and desktop, instead of sitting a touch below it.
Nesting an item under a piece of gear that already has a weight now groups the two, so that gear's own weight stays on its own line — visible and editable — instead of vanishing into the group total.
Renaming a catalog item to your own name now clears the gear type that came with it, instead of leaving the old label stuck on the row for good.
Un-nesting an item out of a group the app created for you now hands its gear type back and removes the leftover group row.
Dragging one weighed item onto another no longer pops the keyboard open on a phone.
The gear type and note button now says what it will actually open, and opens to the field you asked for instead of the one already showing.
Screen readers and voice control can now reach an item's gear type and note button.
"Create a list" from the editor menu no longer drops the list you were on out of your browser history — Back returns to it.
Printed lists no longer show an "Add an item" line under each group.
A renamed catalog item now keeps tracking the catalog's gear type, and an item with your own gear type still tracks the catalog's product name.
A CSV column called "Type" is no longer imported as a gear type — only a "Gear Type" or "Common Name" column is.
An unnamed item no longer shows the placeholder label "Group" unless it really is a group.

added: A “What’s new” page — a running list of features and fixes as they ship.
Search the gear catalog by everyday name — type “tent” to find tents, or “rucksack” and “backpack” to reach the same packs.
Women’s versions across the gear catalog — about a hundred new entries covering footwear, apparel, packs, and sleep.
Nest items one level deep — split a tent into body, fly, poles, and stakes on their own lines, with the group total on the parent row.
Drag an item into or out of a nested group — drag it right to tuck it under the row above, left to pop it back out.
Collapse a group of nested items — a chevron by the group's name hides or shows its children (and remembers your choice), just like a folder.
changed: Combined the Privacy and Terms pages into a single Legal page.
On phones, an item's extra actions (add a note, nest, un-nest) tuck into a ⋯ menu, so each row stays uncluttered — delete and drag stay put.
fixed: Nested items now work in packing mode — you can check them off, and pack progress can reach 100%.
Dragging a grouped item into another folder now carries its nested items along, so weights stay correct.
Copying a list with nested items no longer leaves hidden phantom rows in the copy.
Shared and public lists now show folders in the same order you arranged them.
Reorder items and folders from the keyboard — focus the grip and press the up/down arrows.
Search an accented brand by its plain spelling — typing "Fjallraven" now finds Fjällräven (and Klattermusen finds Klättermusen).

added: Sort any folder by name, heaviest, or lightest — or keep your own manual order.
Import a JSON backup to restore a list. Exporting and re-importing now round-trips a list at full fidelity.
A quiet line in the editor tells you when your list last saved and synced.
fixed: The undo toast is easier to catch — it now stays for ten seconds, pauses when you hover or focus it, and no longer swallows a stray click as it fades.

added: “Your lists” remembers the lists you've opened on this device, and lets you delete one.
A “Copy this list” button on shared lists, so anyone can fork their own editable copy.
Import an existing list straight from a LighterPack link or a CSV file.
A print-friendly layout and a packing checklist with check-off progress, for using a list on the trail.
Add the same item a few times and it folds into one row with a count and a worn split, e.g. “Socks ×3 · 1 worn”.
Build a packing list and share it with a link — no account, no app, no ads.
Live pack-weight totals, with a base / worn / consumable breakdown and a category bar. Weights are optional; a list with none just stays quiet.
A curated, cited gear-weight database with autocomplete, so most items weigh themselves as you type.
Light and dark themes.
